findings.title: arch-08's recommended second HTML Viewer in `explorer` violates ADR-031's own eligibility rule, and is hidden so R14 is not observable
findings.evidence: The arch-08 row recommends 'a second HTML Viewer assigned to explorer in layout 2, hidden by default'. Decision 2 gives explorer a body admitting only tree and table; decision 4 maps html-viewer to document-frame. Running the rule gives 'html-viewer in explorer? False'. StagePage portals only the visible panel per slot, so a hidden instance is unmounted.
findings.consequence: A builder following the recommendation writes a default_assignment the matcher rejects, and a cleared browser does not show two instances mounted, so R14 is not observed.
findings.minimal_fix: Name an eligible slot (primary or secondary in layout 2), hidden by default, and state that R14's test makes it visible by selection.

findings.title: The matcher is a TS pure function; the ADR does not say how pytest computes eligibility
findings.evidence: Decision 4 puts `elements` in PANEL_REGISTRY (TS); the arch-07 row says test_workbench_fit_contracts.py 'must use the matcher' but that test builds its matrix in Python from layout JSON (eligible_slots at lines 1084 and 1854). The ADR rejects TS constants as 'invisible to pytest'.
findings.consequence: arch-07 must guess between a second Python implementation (a drifting second eligibility authority, forbidden by R12), a regex parse plus a Python copy, or a node call.
findings.minimal_fix: State the single implementation site and how Python tests consume it, e.g. a node script emitting the eligibility matrix as JSON, or `elements` kept in a data file both sides read.

findings.title: On shipped data, 'structural match' reduces to a body-kind tag match; bar capacities are deferred
findings.evidence: Step 2 of the decision 4 rule cannot exclude anything shipped; capacities are left to arch-07 with the constraint 'must not exclude any W16 assignment'. The 16/17 result depends only on the body-kind mapping, with primary and secondary each admitting both kinds.
findings.consequence: The rejected alternatives 'capability tags' and 'body kind alone' describe what actually ships, so the text overstates what structure decides.
findings.minimal_fix: State that body kind is the only shipped discriminator, or require one negative bar-capacity test case in arch-07.

findings.title: Claim that the first instance keeping the type id makes a bare type id 'an obvious bug' is backwards
findings.evidence: Decision 5: 'makes a bare type id used where an instance id is meant an obvious bug rather than a silent one'. For every shipped instance instance_id equals the type id.
findings.consequence: A bare type id used as an instance id works silently in every existing test and fails only for -2 instances; plain string aliases do not catch it.
findings.minimal_fix: Reword; require branded types or a standing test exercising a -2 instance of every type.

findings.title: The double header is prevented by contract plus a test, not by construction
findings.evidence: Decision 1 says it 'cannot be produced by a panel that follows the contract'; the mechanism is left to arch-07; checks are grep-style (no .stage-region__header, no import path).
findings.consequence: A panel or sub-app drawing its own bar under another class passes the grep; R13 passes only if the count is by element or role.
findings.minimal_fix: Define the R13 count as header elements and role=banner per slot, not by class, and say the guarantee is a standing test.

findings.title: ADR is silent on REQ-007 W01 (notes strip has no title; only control is the dropdown)
findings.evidence: Every frame has an identity sub-slot filled by the slot and a frame_actions sub-slot; W01 requires no title or label on the strip; the widening list amends W16 and REQ-037 rows, not W01.
findings.consequence: arch-07 either shows a forbidden 'Notes' label and extra buttons on the strip or deviates from W01 without an amendment.
findings.minimal_fix: Make identity and frame_actions optional per frame (compact omits identity), or list W01 among the rows arch-07 amends.

findings.title: 'Undeclared instance is dropped' is ambiguous against workbench-wide instance ids
findings.evidence: Decision 6 drops instance_state entries for undeclared instances; decision 5 makes ids workbench-wide; arch-08 declares html-viewer-2 in layout 2 only.
findings.consequence: If judged per active layout, switching to layout 1 and writing state wipes layout 2's second-viewer tabs, contradicting the kept discard-only-unknown rule.

findings.title: Recommended cross-panel default target amends ADR-029 section 6 point 3 while the ADR claims not to touch it
findings.evidence: Decision 7 recommends 'the visible instance last interacted with' for an omitted key; ADR-029 section 6 points 1 and 3 define get() and an omitted key as the most recently registered handle.
findings.consequence: arch-08 either changes BridgeSlot.get() semantics that phase-wbf-04 and phase-wbf-05 build on, or adds a second default path, with ADR-029 not named as amended.
findings.minimal_fix: State that the rule is a caller-level resolver leaving BridgeSlot.get() as ADR-029 defines it, or name ADR-029 point 3 as amended.

findings.title: A new standing rule ('no migration code, now or later') is added outside the open items
findings.evidence: Decision-3 row of the keep/replace table drops 'in demo week' and states the rule; PLAN-028 decision 3 asks only to keep the persistence posture; the nine open items do not list it.
findings.consequence: The owner is not asked to ratify a rule stronger than ADR-016's wording.
findings.minimal_fix: Add it as an open item or restore the time qualifier.

findings.title: Per-track minmax floors do not say how a spanning slot's floor maps to tracks
findings.evidence: Decision 8 uses minmax(<floor>, <size>fr) per track; secondary spans three rows in layout 1 and three columns in layout 2; strip alone occupies a 0.25fr row.
findings.consequence: arch-09 invents the mapping, and the 'floors fit 1024x768' check depends on it.
findings.minimal_fix: State that a spanning slot's floor applies to the sum of its tracks (or is divided across them).
